s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic illness with fever, diarrhea, and skin lesions
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
History of diverticulosis and colonic polyps
Low-grade fever
Facial lesions initially presented as ill-defined pink patches
Lesions spread to chest, abdomen, back, and left buttock
Mild leukocytosis with normal differential
Mildly elevated transaminase and alkaline phosphatase levels
Negative wound culture
Negative PCR for herpes simplex virus
Negative direct fluorescent antibody assay for varicella-zoster virus
Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration on forehead lesion biopsy
Septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas on right thigh biopsy
Moderate inflammation, edema, erosions, and pseudopolyps in the sigmoid colon on colonoscopy

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of fever, neutrophilic dermatosis, and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerative skin lesions, neutrophilic inflammation, and association with inflammatory bowel disease

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of facial crusted plaques, intradermal neutrophilic inflammation, and ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, moderate inflammation in sigmoid colon, and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Painful subcutaneous nodules, fever, and association with inflammatory bowel disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of new-onset flulike symptoms, low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques, and bloody diarrhea, along with laboratory findings of mild leukocytosis and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation on biopsy, are consistent with Sweet syndrome, a condition characterized by neutrophilic dermatosis and often associated with underlying inflammatory bowel disease or other systemic conditions.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can present with similar skin lesions, the patient's biopsy findings and lack of characteristic ulceration are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis
rejected.why: This is a broader term that encompasses Sweet syndrome, but Sweet syndrome is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, and colonoscopy showed moderate inflammation, the primary presentation is dermatologic, suggesting Sweet syndrome as the more direct diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions and biopsy findings do not match the characteristic presentation of erythema nodosum, which typically involves painful subcutaneous nodules without the specific neutrophilic dermatosis seen in this case.
